newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sets 60 bln bolivar TEM auction Tues.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sets 60 bln bolivar TEM auction Tues.

text.p: The Central Bank of Venezuela announced for Tuesday morning a 40 billion bolivar ($83 million) auction of 177-day "monetary stabilization," or TEM, bills with a 14.33 percent coupon.
The auction was moved to Tuesday from its regular Wednesday slot due to the San Jose bank and market holiday on March 19.
The bank said it would also offer ten billion bolivars ($21 million) in 267-day bills with a 14.58 percent coupon, and another ten billion bolivars of 358-day bills with a 14.85 percent coupon.
One hundred and ten billion bolivars of TEMs are due to mature on Thursday.

Coupons at the Wednesday auction are slightly down from last week's 70 billion bolivar issue. Then 177-, 267- and 358- day notes carried 14.35, 14.61, and 14.87 percent coupons respectively for effective yields that softened as much as 248 basis points at the long end of the curve to 14.33, 16.40, 17.17 percent.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
